title: Baby and child massage
what: A specialist gently massages and stretches your baby's body and does simple exercises with them. This helps muscles and movement develop.
why: For high or low muscle tone, a stiff neck (torticollis), delayed motor development, or as a general strengthening massage, as a pediatrician or neurologist prescribes.
duration: a session usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; a course is usually about 10 sessions
tell_doctor: If your child has a fever, runny nose, or cough
A rash, irritation, or small wounds on the skin
If there is an umbilical hernia
If your child was born early

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Feed your baby no later than 40 to 60 minutes before the massage. It is not done right after a feed.

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: If your child is ill, reschedule the session.

prepare.title: Sleep
prepare.text: Best to pick a time when your baby is usually awake and alert.

bring: Water or a bottle for your child
steps: You undress your baby, and the specialist places them on the changing table
The massage starts with light stroking
Then the arms, legs, back, and belly are worked
Simple exercises and joint movements are done
You stay close and can talk to your baby
feel: Your baby may fuss or cry in the first sessions. That is normal
A correct massage should not hurt
after: Your baby may fall fast asleep
The specialist may show you simple exercises for home
red_flags: Bruises, swelling, or your baby cries when one arm or leg is touched: see a doctor

faq.q: Does a healthy baby need massage?
faq.a: Most often, stroking and play at home are enough. A pediatrician will decide if a course is needed.

faq.q: What if my baby cries the whole session?
faq.a: Tell the specialist. Sometimes a different time or a shorter session helps.

reminders.text: Baby massage tomorrow. Feed your baby no later than an hour before, and bring a blanket and wipes.
